original_question.author: Paul Erdős
original_question.title: Some unconventional problems in number theory

published_finiteness.authors: F. Beukers, T. N. Shorey and R. Tijdeman
published_finiteness.title: Irreducibility of polynomials and arithmetic progressions with equal products of terms
published_finiteness.statement_carrier: Csaba Rakaczki, Acta Arithmetica 110.4 (2003), Theorem B, p. 340
published_finiteness.application: With X=m+5 and Y=n+5, equal degrees 5 and multiplier 4 are outside the stated infinite-family exceptions.
published_finiteness.boundary: Published finiteness of rational/integer solutions is prior work; it does not supply an admissible solution list or usable cutoff in the consulted statement.

contract.offsets: natural numbers including zero; all five factors are positive
contract.inverse: For every natural m, (m+2)^5<P(m)<(m+3)^5; any solution to P(m)=T has m=floor(T^(1/5))-2.
contract.compact_certificate: At n=from+i, root R is certified by R^5<=4P(n)<(R+1)^5. The only candidate is m=R-2; signed difference is P(m)-4P(n).

record_extrema.basis: linear read of the already-retained compact records; no product or root recalculation

retention.full_expanded_point_objects: Only first and last expanded classifications are retained; every point's root/candidate and difference are retained compactly.
retention.root_bracket_powers: Root powers and gaps are explicit for the first and last point. Other powers are determined by the retained root and input index; every point's bracket was checked during its one classification.
retention.resumed_scans: Each record is tied to its n. A later worker can consume these records without repeating the root iteration.

evidence_scope.combined_recorded_interval: 0<=n<=1010000 combines the existing accepted receipt with this disjoint new interval; the older prefix was not rerun.
